proof.pattern: day-tier ENTRY-TRIGGER: FADE: no failed wall-sweep yet \(close

expected_rate: once per qualifying name per 2-minute tick while it waits; ~600 lines per session (10/20 had 799 would_consider decisions, e.g. ~220 each for AMZN/GOOGL/TSLA)
reversal: any change in Day-tier trigger outcomes (ENTER/WAIT, direction, entry_ref, target) versus the same inputs before the change, or a new exception in compute_entry_trigger
baseline_exempt_reason: The proof line is new text that only this change writes ('FADE: no failed wall-sweep yet (close'); the old code never logged FADE waits, so it has zero matches before ship. No change_id tag is added to keep the line in the existing ENTRY-TRIGGER format.
